item.title: TimeMachine: Fine-Grained Facial Age Editing With Identity Preservation
item.description: With the advancement of generative models, facial image editing has made significant progress. However, achieving fine-grained age editing while preserving personal identity remains a challenging task. In this paper, we propose TimeMachine, a unified diffusion-based framework for accurate facial age editing with identity preservation. TimeMachine employs fine-grained age conditions and a Multi-Cross-Attention module to decouple the dedicated age and identity conditions. This branch-wise design enables controllable age transformation while maintaining identity consistency. Furthermore, we introduce an Age Classifier Guidance (ACG) module that predicts age embeddings from latent denoising features without reconstructing images during training. This lightweight training-only predictor provides additional age-related supervision and is removed during inference. To support large-scale training, we construct HFFA (High-quality Fine-grained Facial-Age), a million-scale collection of high-resolution face images annotated with captions, identity embeddings, MiVOLO-estimated numerical ages, and age embeddings. Extensive experiments across five public face datasets demonstrate that TimeMachine achieves superior age accuracy and identity preservation relative to the evaluated baselines, with consistent conclusions across five age estimators. The project page is available at https://miyilin2003.github.io/TimeMachine

item.title: Break It Down to Build It Up: Unified Face Attack Detection via Adaptive Fine-Grained Knowledge Reorganization
item.description: Face images have become ubiquitous in modern society, but are vulnerable to both physical attacks (presentation attacks) that spoof identities and digital attacks (DeepFakes) that manipulate facial appearance. These attacks threaten security systems by bypassing biometric authentication and can be used to create realistic fake media for disinformation or fraud. Previous research has largely focused on detecting either physical or digital attacks in isolation. Given that physical and digital attacks both produce fake faces that differ statistically from real ones, learning them in a shared representation space becomes feasible. Recent studies suggest that jointly modeling both attack types, i.e., Unified Face Attack Detection (UAD), can enhance detection performance. Existing UAD methods, however, typically employ coarse training strategies that ignore subtle fine-grained cues and inter-attack correlations. Thus, we propose a novel two-stage framework, namely Break It Down to Build It Up (B2B): a Break-Down stage that learns fine-grained local features from facial patches, followed by a Build-Up stage that adaptively reorganizes this knowledge across attack types. Extensive experiments on ten public face-attack datasets demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art methods. Beyond the promising results, our analysis reveals that many attacks produce similar forensic patterns (e.g., face-swapping and 3D-mask), suggesting deeper connections across attack types. This observation provides new insights for the design of future detection methods. types. Code is available at https://github.com/Allen-hcyuan/B2B
